title: Joe Fazer's Workout program for Skinny guys trying to get Bigger review
summary: Review of Joe Fazer's A/B full-body program for skinny beginners. He likes the pull-ups, dips and arm isolation but criticises the crammed day B (squat, deadlift and rows together, deadlift placed third) and repetitive 3x5s, and fixes it with a third day (A-C-B) that spreads the volume.
claims: Young influencers carry responsibility because their young audience follows idols blindly; he reviews them with more leeway than self-proclaimed experts
A/B templates are minimalist by default: two days force exercises to repeat, which suits novices who gain from repetition and simplicity, and can be run just twice a week
Training four days a week on an A/B split hits the limits of minimalism; three-day templates become more interesting
Squat 3x5 is fine for novices; they do not need evolving rep ranges
A program of only compound lifts smells of Starting Strength and powerlifting, which is wrong for a hypertrophy goal
Including pull-ups beats most novice programs; 3 sets to failure suits novices who cannot do many reps
Superset pull-ups and dips; most novices have poor cardiovascular fitness and it will challenge them
Barbell curls 3x8-10 is an excellent range for biceps; arm isolation saves an otherwise compound-only program
Add abs, calves and neck at the end of sessions; started early, they pay off three or four years later

Do not repeat 3x5 squats every session: vary the range (3x8, 3x10) or use variations like pause squats, lunges or anything you will stick to; people told to squat 3x a week often quit after two months
Incline bench 3x8 is a hybrid of horizontal and vertical pressing that gives more chest; some may prefer overhead press
The deadlift must open the workout, never be third; 3x5 squats plus 3x5 deadlifts in one novice session is too much and an injury risk
After a heavy pull, the knee flexion should be light with more reps, e.g. pause squats 3x10
Rows after squats and deadlifts are a bad idea: the lower back is fried and the row is technically and muscularly demanding
Do the second curl session at 3x5-7 or 3x4-6 to taste a different intensity
Close-grip bench can stay on the incline day if the incline becomes 3x12

Fix: add a workout C (order A-C-B) opening with a hip hinge or rows, then incline or overhead press, close-grip bench, long head triceps, chin-ups, shrugs and lateral raises; day B opens with deadlifts then a lighter squat variation
Back hyperextensions 3-4x12 teach novices to pull with their legs and build the lower back; for advanced lifters they waste tonnage
Spreading the same work over three days raises frequency and volume quality and shortens sessions; two versus three gym days makes little difference in commitment
Cramming too much into two days risks overuse injuries and burnout, especially for skinny guys with limited capacity
exercises: calisthenics for novices who cannot do many reps
lower back already fried; demanding lift
novice hip hinge teaching leg drive and building lower back
